A.note: Flat green plain with two tan rectangles of tiny tent dots and a few tree specks. The fortified rock is a small, distant blob and the ships are tiny dots. The sea and sky are pleasant, but the ground is a flat colour field and the camps look pasted on.

B.note: Same layout as A. The ground has more grass texture and the tree clusters are denser and more natural, so it reads a little more like a real place. The camps are still flat tan slabs with dot tents, and the rock and ships are still far away.

C.note: Close top-down view. The tents are identical white blocks laid out in a perfect grid on flat tan rectangles, which looks like a board game. The trench line is the one believable element. There is no horizon, no fortress and no sense of place.

D.note: Best terrain: a textured hillside with scrub, a natural horizon and atmospheric depth. The camps are still pale gridded rectangles that look pasted on. No fortress or sea is visible, so the siege context is missing.

why: D has the most convincing terrain, lighting and depth, and B has better vegetation than A, while C's toy-like grid of identical blocks reads worst.
top_fix_for_best: Replace the flat grid camp rectangles in D with irregular clusters of tents at varied sizes and rotations. Add cook-fire smoke, tracks and trampled ground, and tiny figures and wagons. Also put the fortified rock or the sea in frame so the siege reads.
